payload.text:
Project: Clinical SOAP patient data collector — Inpatient + Outpatient

Goal
Build a classic-UI HTML web application for collecting inpatient and outpatient SOAP-format data that:
- Has a landing/home page with two options: "Inpatient form" and "Outpatient form". Each option routes to its respective form page.
- Supports day-by-day inpatient progress + vitals + labs + treatment entries and allows exporting a patient's case to PDF or Word.
- Follows the attached paper proforma layout (Patient Data Collection Proforma, 4 pages). Reference file provided.

Users & Roles
- Clinician (data entry): can create/edit patient records.
- Pharmacist / Reviewer: can add pharm-care notes (ADR, interventions).
- Viewer: read-only.
- Optional: Admin for user management.

Security & Compliance
- HTTPS, per-session auth with role-based access.
- Audit trail (who edited which field & timestamp).
- Data export and deletion governed by admin (log deletions).
- Optionally support Indian privacy/gov standards or HIPAA-like controls (encrypted at rest).

Primary UI / Navigation
- Home: two large cards/buttons — "Inpatient" and "Outpatient". Clicking navigates to respective form.
- Classic, uncluttered UI (desktop-first, responsive).
- Left column: patient header summary (Name, MRN/admission no, age, gender, dept/ward, consultant, date of admission/discharge). Right/main area: form.

Inpatient form — required structure & fields
(Use short field keys for DB; display labels are full words with hover hints.)

Header (single-row)
- patient_name: text (required)
- mrn: text / auto-generate optional
- age_years: integer
- gender: enum {Male, Female, Other}
- department_ward: text
- consultant: text / select from staff list
- date_of_admission: date
- date_of_discharge: date (nullable)
- provisional_admitting_diagnosis: text
- chief_complaints: multiline text

Daily Progress / Prognosis & Treatment (core)
- Provide a day selector (Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, …). On first entry, show Day 1 with default fields 1–4 visible.
- Option: "Add new day" -> creates next day record. When selecting an existing day, load that day's entries.
- If user chooses "Auto-load previous day's 1–4", prefill that day's chief complaint, conscious state, vitals, and treatments with an option to "Continue same treatment" checkbox for each medication.

For each day record include:

1) date_of_entry: date (default = today)
2) conscious_coherent: enum {Yes, No} (checkbox UI)
3) chief_complaint_of_the_day: multiline text

4) patient_vitals: repeatable timestamped vitals row(s)
   - vitals_time: time (or datetime)
   - pulse_pr_bpm: integer (bpm)
   - respiratory_rate_rr_bpm: integer (bpm)
   - spo2_percent: integer (0–100)
   - systolic_bp_mmHg: integer
   - diastolic_bp_mmHg: integer
   - random_blood_sugar_rbs_mg_dl: number
   - fasting_blood_sugar_fbs_mg_dl: number
   - postprandial_ppbs_mg_dl: number
   - notes: small text (e.g., "pre-prandial", "post-meal")
   - Allow adding multiple vitals rows per day (for trend).

5) organ_system_exams:
   - cvs_text: multiline
   - rs_text: multiline
   - gcs_eye: integer 1–4
   - gcs_verbal: integer 1–5
   - gcs_motor: integer 1–6
   - gcs_total: computed, display-only

6) labs & investigations
   - Sidebar: "Add lab tests for this day" modal with checkboxes of common tests and free-text:
       * CBC, LFT, RFT, pancreatic enzymes (amylase/lipase), serum electrolytes, lipid profile, thyroid profile, HbA1c, urine analysis, iron profile, malaria, typhoid (Widal), dengue, cultures, ABG, 2D-echo, X-ray, CT, MRI, USG, ECG.
   - Each selected lab gets an input row: test_name, value, units, sample_time/date.
   - Allow uploading lab report files (PDF/image) and storing link.

7) Specialty structured inputs (optional if present)
   - 2D_echocardiogram: structured fields (EF%, LVH, RWMA, others) + file upload + free text.
   - ABG: pH, PaCO2, PaO2, HCO3, BE, SaO2.
   - ECG impression: text + image upload.

8) Assessment scales
   - Pain scale numeric 0–10
   - Others (addable): create scale_name, value.

Treatment section (per day)
- Treatment items are repeatable rows with:
   - rx_symbol: display icon
   - seq_no: integer (auto-increment for ordering)
   - dosage_form: enum {Tab, Cap, Inj, Nebul, Syrup, Ointment, IV, Other}
   - route: enum {PO, IV, IM, SC, Nebulized, Topical, PR, Other}
   - medication_brand: text (optional)
   - medication_generic: text (required)
   - indication: text
   - dose: text (e.g., "500 mg")
   - frequency: text (e.g., "OD", "BD", "TDS", "q6h", "PRN")
   - timing_relation: enum {Before Food (BF), After Food (AF), With Food, Empty Stomach, Irrelevant}
   - start_date: date
   - end_date: date (nullable)
   - frequency_notes: text (e.g., "q4h PRN for pain")
   - route_notes: text
   - free_text_treatment: boolean (if true, show a single free text area to enter non-drug treatment e.g., physiotherapy, wound care)
   - continue_from_previous_day: boolean (if checked, mark visually; default unchecked)
- UI: an "Add treatment row" button. Each row has a quick-toggle "Continue same treatment as previous day".

Drug chart (summary table)
- Mirroring PDF table: columns => Sl. No, Brand Name, Generic Name, Indication, Dose, ROA, Frequency, Administration Start & End date.
- Provide export-friendly table and allow printing.

Pharmacy / Clinical review
- pharmaceutical_care_issues: multiline (ADR, DI, rationality, interventions)
- discussion_case_specific: multiline (etiology, treatment options)
- ADR capture: structured ADR form with suspected drug, description, severity, outcome, action taken.

Other features
- Attachments: upload files (imaging, reports) per patient and per day.
- Free text headings: allow clinician to add headings (chest, knee, bone X-ray, etc.) with a text box as requested.
- Shortcuts: allow user to type shortcuts (RBS, PPBS, FBS, RR, PR, SpO2, GCS) that expand; provide auto-complete and field mapping.
- Quick-lab sidebar: allow picking multiple tests (points 5–9) to show inputs for that day.
- Ability to choose which default fields (1–4) appear on the day form via a settings panel.

Export / Printing
- Export patient record (single admission) as:
  - PDF formatted like the printed proforma (export template that places header, progress chart, drug chart, pharm care & discussion).
  - Word (.docx) with structured sections.
- Also support CSV/Excel export for data analysis.

Data model suggestion (simplified JSON)
- patient: { id, name, mrn, age, gender, dept, consultant, admission_date, discharge_date, diagnosis, allergies, social_history, weight, height }
- encounters: [ { day_number, date, conscious, chief_complaint, vitals: [], labs: [], treatments: [], echo: {}, abg: {}, notes: {pharm, discussion} } ]
- attachments: [ { file_id, filename, date_uploaded, linked_to: patient|encounter } ]

UX / Validation rules
- Required: patient_name, date_of_admission, at least one chief complaint or diagnosis.
- Vitals numeric ranges: PR 20–250; RR 5–60; SpO₂ 0–100; BP realistic bounds.
- GCS components validate ranges.
- For dose fields, allow free-text but encourage structured input; provide unit hints.

Optional advanced integrations (recommend)
- Drug database integration for autocomplete & interaction checks (open-source or licensed).
- Use FHIR resources (Patient, Observation, MedicationStatement, Condition) for future interoperability / NDHM compatibility.
- LOINC/SNOMED mapping for lab & problem codification.
- Role-based templates (ward vs ICU) and custom templates per specialty.

Acceptance criteria / tests
1. Create inpatient record, add Day 1, enter vitals (two timestamps), labs, and 3 treatments; export to PDF and Word — all fields present and aligned.
2. Add Day 2 and use "Continue same treatment" to copy previous treatments; ability to edit copied rows.
3. Add ABG and 2D-echo structured results and upload files; view files in patient attachments.
4. Pharmacist can add ADR entry; audit shows who added it.
5. Export drug chart contains all medications with start/end dates.

Non-functional
- Responsive, tested on Chrome/Edge desktop.
- Print-friendly CSS.
- Usability: keyboard access, tab order for rapid use.
- Save-as-draft autosave every 30 seconds.

Deliverables
- Frontend: HTML/CSS/JS (or React) with specified forms, plus PDF/Word export functionality.
- Backend: REST endpoints for patient, encounter, labs, treatments, attachments.
- Simple DB schema (Postgres recommended).
- README with deployment instructions, sample test data, and mapping of field keys to display labels.

**Building the Framework**

I'm currently focused on the React component structure, ensuring a solid foundation for the data collector. TypeScript integration is underway, adding type safety to the form fields. Tailwind CSS is proving efficient for rapid prototyping of the proforma layout.


**Developing Core Features**

I've been concentrating on the core React components. I've defined the key features like day-by-day progress tracking, vitals, labs, treatments, pharmacy reviews, and PDF export. Components are being outlined for Sidebar, Layout, VitalsRow, LabRow, TreatmentRow, and related elements. TypeScript interfaces are progressing nicely for the complex data model, which will be critical for managing the varied data.  A mock persistence layer using localStorage is also in development.


**Prioritizing Print Functionality**

I'm now zeroing in on the "Print" view, leveraging CSS for a clean and browser-friendly output. My focus now is on implementing a print-specific stylesheet to ensure readability. I'm prioritizing user-friendly features like patient summaries and an easily expandable shortcut feature (e.g., "RBS" expanding to "Random Blood Sugar") to streamline form completion. I'll need to define the main page header with patient demographics like name, MRN, age, and gender.


**Organizing Data Structure**

I'm now diving into the main data structure.  I'm structuring the app with key areas: Basic Info, Daily Progress, Drug Chart, and Review/Discussion tabs. Daily progress will feature a day selector for data entry, including vitals, exams, and labs. The drug chart will show an aggregated view of medications. Review section will capture notes on adverse drug reactions (ADRs) and pharmacist insights. I'm moving toward XML generation.

**Reviewing UI Implementation**

Okay, so I'm considering how to integrate that "Continue same treatment" option directly within each treatment row of the Inpatient Form's Daily Progress section.  I'm exploring a checkbox or a simple toggle switch as the most user-friendly approach. It seems the best fit given the repetitive nature of daily treatments.


**Analyzing Treatment UI Integration**

I've been examining the `InpatientForm.tsx` code closely, focusing on how treatment rows are rendered. The existing `Treatment` interface includes a `continue_from_previous` field, which is promising. I'm now thinking about integrating a UI element, likely a checkbox, directly within each treatment row to manage this "continue" state. The challenge is ensuring it's visually unobtrusive yet easily accessible and understandable within the context of the existing form layout.


**Adding "Continue" Functionality**

I'm now focusing on integrating the "continue from previous" functionality into the treatment rows. I'm going to add a checkbox to each treatment input group.  The challenge will be wiring it to the `onChange` event to update the `treatments` state, ensuring it plays nicely with the existing `updateActiveEncounter` function.  I need to ensure the checkbox's state accurately reflects the `continue_from_previous` value for each treatment.


**Finalizing Treatment Row UI**

I've got the checkbox rendering within the treatment row, and wired to the `continue_from_previous` state! The accompanying text is small but readable. Now, I need to focus on ensuring the dose and frequency fields are fully functional, properly updating the state on user input. I'll integrate the input `value` and `onChange` hooks for those fields, as they're critical to the overall functionality.


**Improving Form Functionality**

I'm now prioritizing making the form fully functional while integrating the "continue same treatment" option. While not strictly requested, fixing the dose and frequency input is a high-impact adjustment. After a review of `InpatientForm.tsx`, I've verified that the necessary state field exists. Now I can move to updating the input components. I'll focus on lines 350-380 of `InpatientForm.tsx` to get an idea of where to begin.


**Implementing Dose/Frequency Inputs**

I'm now integrating the dose and frequency inputs, focusing on updating the `InpatientForm.tsx` file to incorporate the necessary input components and state management. I've located lines 350-380, and I'm currently figuring out how to map the state variables. My goal is to streamline the form for the user to make it easier to add a treatment.


**Integrating Medication Inputs**

I'm now focusing on integrating the medication inputs. I'm going to add a medication input for the treatment, and also a button to delete. I've been reviewing the code for guidance on input updates. I've ensured a functional way to modify the treatments. The new function will also update the encounter.  I'm making progress in making these additions.


**Completing Treatment Functionality**

I've integrated the dose and frequency inputs, wired them to the correct state variables.  I also implemented the medication and delete functionality.  I've reviewed the existing input update system to streamline the form for the user to make it easier to add a treatment.  The new function also updates the encounter.


**Polishing UI Implementation**

Now I'm polishing the UI implementation of the treatment continuation. I'm focusing on refining the visual cues and ensuring that the checkbox's state accurately reflects the underlying data. I also want to make sure the checkbox visually communicates its state and its role in the treatment row. This will involve fine-tuning the CSS and verifying its behavior with the existing form's interactions.


**Adding 'Uncheck' Functionality**

I've integrated the toggle switch successfully and can now uncheck it or check it later. I added the necessary function to allow users to uncheck it manually. Now, I'm focusing on ensuring its behavior integrates seamlessly with the form's overall functionality. This involves testing how the state change impacts the "continue" functionality downstream, ensuring no unexpected side effects.
